title: SAGE: A Unified Framework for Generalizable Object State Recognition with S

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract and Introduction ("On some datasets, SAGE achieves up to 14.6% relative precision gain on novel state recognition")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The tables in the paper do not support a 14.6% relative precision improvement. On ChangeIt novel objects (Table 2a), State Pre@1 is 0.49 vs VidOSC 0.43, giving ~13.95% relative gain. On HowToChange novel objects (Table 2b), the changes are even smaller. No reported number yields exactly 14.6%, making the claim unsubstantiated.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix, Table A9 caption ("We conduct Student’s t-test to evaluate the statistical significance of the results of our main experiments in Table 6.")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The caption references Table 6, but the statistical tests compare SAGE against LFC, MTC, and VidOSC using metrics that correspond to Tables 1 and 2. Table 6 only evaluates different vision-language models and does not contain baseline comparisons. The incorrect table reference misleads readers about the source of the tested data.

The ablation study reports a single 'Pre@1' score for the ChangeIt dataset, but the standard evaluation uses two separate metrics (State Pre@1 and Trans. Pre@1). The paper does not define how this single metric is computed nor how it relates to the earlier results. This missing definition makes the ablation numbers impossible to interpret and compare properly, undermining the conclusions drawn from the ablation.
